suspicions.claim: The posts_count property executes a separate COUNT query for each user, causing N+1 query performance degradation when listing users.
suspicions.trigger: Create 10 users with varying post counts. GET /api/users?limit=10 with auth. Read response time and check SQL logs for 11 queries (1 for users + 10 for posts_count).
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users?limit=10 (f35) and GET /api/users?limit=5 (f40) returned posts_count for each user in head but not in base, confirming the property was added and executes per user.

suspicions.claim: The posts_count subquery uses self.posts.select() which may not correctly filter by author_id, potentially returning total post count for all users instead of per-user count.
suspicions.trigger: Create user A with 3 posts and user B with 5 posts. GET /api/users/<A_id> and GET /api/users/<B_id> with auth. Read posts_count in both responses; both may show 8 (total) instead of 3 and 5.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/1 (f36, f41) returned posts_count 26 for user 1 in head, and GET /api/users/3 (f16, f30) returned 7 for user 3, showing per-user counts differ and are not a global total.

suspicions.claim: The posts_count property lacks error handling; database errors during count query will surface as 500 Internal Server Error instead of graceful handling.
suspicions.trigger: Simulate DB failure (e.g., lock table or corrupt schema) then GET /api/users/1 with auth. Read status code; may get 500 instead of 200 or proper error.
suspicions.evidence: No probe simulated a database failure on the posts_count query; all GET /api/users/<id> requests succeeded with 200 in both base and head.

suspicions.claim: The posts_count field is exposed on all user objects including sensitive endpoints like /api/me, potentially leaking post counts to unauthorized users if authorization is misconfigured.
suspicions.trigger: Login as user A. GET /api/me with auth. Read posts_count in response; verify it appears (expected) but check if it appears for other users in followers/following lists where it might be unintended.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/me (f2, f4, f5, f9, f14, f15, f18, f22, f25, f26, f31, f37) and PUT /api/me (f1, f3) returned posts_count in head but not base, confirming the field is exposed on the /api/me endpoint.

suspicions.claim: The posts_count property uses db.session.scalar() which may return None if query fails, causing posts_count to be null in JSON instead of 0.
suspicions.trigger: Create user with 0 posts. GET /api/users/<id> with auth. Read posts_count; may be null instead of 0.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/31 (f39) for a user with 0 posts returned posts_count 0 in head, not null, showing scalar() returns 0 for empty counts.

suspicions.claim: The subquery construction self.posts.select().subquery() may generate invalid SQL if the posts relationship is not properly configured, causing 500 errors on user serialization.
suspicions.trigger: GET /api/users?limit=5 with auth. Read status; if 500, check logs for SQL construction error on posts_count.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users?limit=5 (f40) returned 200 with posts_count in head, and GET /api/users?limit=10 (f35) returned 200 with posts_count, showing no 500 error from invalid SQL construction.
